Springfield High School Physics (Grade 10) — Homework Assignment
Name: Class: Section: Time: 40 min
Roll No: Date: Max Marks: 40
Instructions: • All questions are compulsory. • Draw diagrams neatly with a pencil. • Show all steps in numerical problems.

questions.question_text: Q1. State Newton's second law of motion and write its formula.
questions.answer_text: It states that force equals rate of change of momentum. Formula: F = m x a

questions.question_text: Q2. A body of mass 5 kg accelerates at 3 m/s^2. Find the force.
questions.answer_text: F = m x a = 5 x 3 = 15 N

questions.question_text: Q3. Draw a free-body diagram of a block resting on a rough horizontal surface being pushed by force
Q4. Define kinetic energy and give its SI unit.
questions.answer_text: Energy possessed by a body due to its motion. SI unit: joule (J).

questions.question_text: Q5. Complete the motion table for uniform acceleration a = 2 m/s^2, starting from rest:
Q6. Calculate the pressure exerted by a force of 100 N on an area of 5 m^2.
Q7. Using Ohm's law, find the current when V = 12 V and R = 3 ohm.
questions.answer_text: I = V x R = 12 x 3 = 36 A

questions.question_text: Q8. Explain the term 'inertia' with one everyday example.
questions.answer_text: Inertia is the tendency of a body to resist a change in its state of motion. Example: passengers lurch forward when a bus stops suddenly.

questions.question_text: Q9. Write the formula for momentum and calculate it for m = 3 kg, v = 4 m/s.
questions.answer_text: p = m x v = 3 x 4 = 12 kg.m/s

questions.question_text: Q10State the law of conservation of energy.
questions.answer_text:
Energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only transformed from one form to another.
– End of Physics Paper –
